claims.claim_text: The U.S. advanced-compute control regime was revised repeatedly between October 2022 and December 2024.
claims.interpretation: The policy should be analyzed as an evolving sequence, not as a single unchanged intervention.
claims.known_limitation: Rule changes establish legal scope but do not by themselves establish real-world technological effect.

evidence.exact_text: The October 2022 interim final rule added controls for certain advanced-computing items, semiconductor-manufacturing items, and specified supercomputer and semiconductor-manufacturing end uses.
evidence.locator: 87 FR 62186, Summary and Supplementary Information § I
evidence.reviewer_note: Human-entered data point checked against the cited official rule.

evidence.exact_text: The October 2023 interim final rule updated and corrected the advanced-computing and supercomputer controls adopted in 2022.
evidence.reviewer_note: Human-entered data point checked against the cited official rule.

evidence.exact_text: The December 2024 interim final rule added foreign-produced direct-product provisions and refined advanced-computing and semiconductor-manufacturing controls.
evidence.locator: 89 FR 96790, Summary and Supplementary Information § I
evidence.reviewer_note: Human-entered data point checked against the cited official rule.

claims.claim_text: The selected MOFCOM records show a shift from public objection to U.S. semiconductor export controls in October 2023 to U.S.-specific dual-use export controls in December 2024.
claims.interpretation: The selected official record shows a shift in instruments—from an official public response to U.S.-specific dual-use controls—without proving economic effect.
claims.known_limitation: Official announcements establish stated policy and legal measures, not the scale of enforcement, compliance, or downstream supply impact.

evidence.exact_text: MOFCOM expressed strong dissatisfaction and firm opposition to the October 2023 U.S. rules and said China would take all necessary measures to safeguard its legitimate rights and interests.
evidence.reviewer_note: Descriptive English data point; consult the original Chinese text.

evidence.exact_text: Announcement No. 46 prohibited exports of dual-use items to U.S. military users or for military uses. Its second numbered provision generally denied licensing for relevant gallium-, germanium-, antimony-, and superhard-material dual-use items to the United States and subjected graphite dual-use items to stricter end-user and end-use review.
evidence.reviewer_note: Descriptive English data point; consult the original Chinese text.

claims.claim_text: As of 2026-09-03, implementation of the second numbered provision of MOFCOM Announcement No. 46 is suspended from 2025-11-09 until 2026-11-27; Announcement No. 72 does not suspend the rest of No. 46.
claims.interpretation: Current-status checking changes the comparison: adoption and continuing operation are separate propositions.
claims.known_limitation: The suspension applies only to the second numbered provision and should not be generalized to the entire 2024 announcement.

evidence.exact_text: MOFCOM Announcement No. 72 states that implementation of the second numbered provision of Announcement No. 46 is suspended from November 9, 2025 through November 27, 2026.
evidence.reviewer_note: Verified against MOFCOM’s operative text on 2026-09-03; scope limited to the second numbered provision.

claims.claim_text: MOFCOM Announcement No. 72 suspended all of Announcement No. 46 during the stated period.
claims.interpretation: Rejected as an overbroad reading: the operative text suspends only the second numbered provision.
claims.known_limitation: The English wording is descriptive; the official Chinese text controls, and the legal-status check is dated 2026-09-03.

evidence.exact_text: Announcement No. 72 suspends implementation of the second numbered provision of Announcement No. 46 for the stated period, rather than suspending the announcement in full.
evidence.reviewer_note: Counterevidence to the overbroad proposition; descriptive translation checked against the operative Chinese text on 2026-09-03.

definitions.definition: Computing capability and covered items falling within the technical and end-use scope of the policy instruments being studied.
definitions.scope: Working definition for this demonstration corpus; not a universal threshold.
definitions.rationale: Avoid treating a changing regulatory threshold as a timeless technical category.

definitions.definition: The operative state described by the most recent official instrument included in the research record.
definitions.scope: Initial definition for the public demonstration corpus.
definitions.rationale: Created to distinguish the adoption date from later implementation status.

definitions.definition: The operative state described by the most recent official instrument, reported with an explicit as-of date and limited to the provisions that instrument actually changes.
definitions.scope: Revised definition for the public demonstration corpus.
definitions.rationale: A later announcement suspended only one provision, so the definition now requires an as-of date and provision-level scope.

comparisons.rationale: The first claim describes the historical shift through adoption in 2024; the second checks the later operating status of one provision through 2026.
The scoped claim follows the provision-level operative text; the rejected claim incorrectly generalizes the suspension to the whole announcement.

decisions.before_state: The 2024 measure was treated as continuing unchanged.
decisions.after_state: The second numbered provision is suspended from 2025-11-09 through 2026-11-27; the rest of Announcement No. 46 remains in force.
decisions.rationale: Announcement No. 72 changed the current-status assessment without undoing the historical fact that Announcement No. 46 was adopted.
